createfurnaceengine.ponder.furnace_engin: Furnace Engines use a running Furnace, Blast Furnace, or Smoker as their heat source
Attach the Engine to one of the furnace's side faces
The front face is reserved for accessing the furnace and cannot hold an Engine
Only one Furnace Engine can be attached to each furnace
The Engine leaves one empty block between its Head and the output Flywheel
Hold a Flywheel and right-click the Engine to use its placement guide
The Flywheel axis must be perpendicular to the Engine and may not stand upright
Wear Engineer's Goggles and scroll the value box to choose the rotation direction
The Flywheel and Crank reverse together
The Engine remains stopped while the furnace is idle
When the furnace starts, the Engine begins at 1 RPM
It climbs by about a twelfth of the target every 15 ticks, until the target RPM is reached
Stress capacity scales with the current speed: RPM multiplied by SU per RPM
An adjacent configured Heat Sink switches the Engine to its Heat Sink RPM and SU/RPM settings
By default, any Copper Block touching one of the furnace's six faces is a Heat Sink
